title: Love Addiction
description: Love, celebrated by poets and artists, inspires us and gives us a sense of fulfillment. However, when love turns into a pathological need, it can erode your sense of self and make it difficult to build healthy relationships—especially if you struggle with low self-esteem. True happiness and fulfillment can be found by learning to regulate your mood and enjoying pleasures that don’t depend on having a partner.

texts: Love is a magnificent feeling, celebrated by poets, artists, and musicians. It inspires us, lifts our spirits, and gives us a sense of fulfillment.
It is only natural for each of us to want to love and be loved.
However, if your idea of love is based on the belief, “I can’t be truly happy or fulfilled without a partner. I need to be loved to be happy,” this is already a sign of dependency.
What does it mean to be dependent on love?
It means love has become a pathological need—something you feel you cannot be happy without.

<important>You suffer from a perceived lack of love and expect someone else to fill that void. You are convinced that your life will only become better, more interesting, and more meaningful once a partner arrives to make you feel needed, significant, and whole.</important>
This kind of dependency is an unhelpful state that undermines your personality, your self-esteem, and your ability to build healthy relationships.
The causes of love dependency vary, but they often have roots in childhood or adolescence.
People with low self-esteem are particularly vulnerable—those who fear loneliness, focus on their flaws, and doubt their own strength and abilities.
Low self-esteem stemming from childhood is often experienced as a sense of inadequacy.
When parents provide little attention and a child lacks parental love, that person may seek those feelings in partners during adulthood, forming dependent relationships.
Take the example of Victoria, 28, who spends her evenings and weekends in despair because she believes: “I can only be happy in a relationship. Without a man, I am nothing.”
For her, being loved is as essential as breathing. This level of neediness often pushes people away.
While analyzing her beliefs, Victoria wrote down the downsides and benefits of her way of thinking.
The downsides were:
• This belief makes me feel despondent because I am alone.
• I lose the desire to do anything, explore the world, or pursue hobbies.
• Because of this, I feel lazy and unhappy.
• It triggers feelings of self-pity.
• It strips me of pride and confidence, making me feel envious of others and deeply disappointed.
Then, she wrote down the benefits of this belief:
• The hope of finding a partner, finding love, and feeling secure.
• It gives me a sense of purpose and meaning in life.
How real are these benefits?
For years, Victoria believed she couldn’t live without a man, yet this very belief hasn’t helped her find the partner she desires.
<q author="Seneca">“True happiness lies in being content with oneself.”</q>
Victoria realized she was placing too much importance on men, which actually prevented her from attracting them.
She also realized that dependent people often come across as too demanding, which makes building relationships harder.
She saw that people who find happiness within themselves are often more attractive to others because they radiate joy and confidence.

<important>Love dependency hinders healthy relationships. By expressing a need for another person to achieve your own happiness, you are subconsciously communicating: “Love me, because I am nothing on my own.” Such relationships are unlikely to be healthy.</important>

Even if you are in a relationship, holding these beliefs makes it unlikely to be a healthy one. You end up relying entirely on a specific person—whom you subconsciously view as the source of your happiness—to be by your side.

And you may be willing to do anything. When you don’t get the “dose” of emotion and feeling you need, you might pressure your partner to feel loved, or start fantasizing about finding that “perfect love” elsewhere.
You will always feel like something is missing or “not quite right,” because you have placed the responsibility for your well-being on someone else.
It’s incredibly important to learn how to regulate your mood and find happiness within yourself. This will allow you to feel just as alive when you’re alone as when you’re with a loved one.
But you might think, “That sounds great, but it doesn’t feel realistic. Being alone means being an emotional failure.”
Many believe that love is what drives the world. You see it in commercials, hear it in pop songs, and read it in poetry. But in reality, love is far from the only path to a happy and fulfilling life.
Being alone is not the same as being unhappy. Most of life’s pleasures can be enjoyed on your own.
For example, when you listen to your favorite music, dance, walk through beautiful places, read a book, or eat ice cream. You don’t need company to experience joy.
<q author="Oscar Wilde">Self-love is the beginning of a lifelong romance.</q>
The number of pleasures you can enjoy alone is endless. This means you have access to many sources of joy, regardless of whether someone is by your side.
Think about it—what is your list of pleasures? What can you do to treat yourself?
Sometimes we strive so hard for the perfect relationship and the idea of a grand romance that we lose sight of what we actually need to experience true love.

exercise.title: How to overcome love addiction?
exercise.description: This article explores happiness and the beliefs associated with love and relationships. It explains that happiness can be achieved in many ways and offers techniques to change unhelpful beliefs related to loneliness. The article teaches you how to find joy in everyday things and grow as an individual, regardless of whether you are in a romantic relationship.

texts: Relationships and love can bring immense joy and happiness to your life, but they aren’t the only way.
Happiness is a complex and multifaceted process, and everyone has the right to choose their own path to achieve it.
So, if your life doesn’t include a romantic relationship right now, it doesn’t make it any less meaningful.
Changing your beliefs takes significant effort; it is a long and demanding process.
But we are confident that by using the following recommendations and techniques, you can overcome love addiction and learn to be happy both in a relationship and on your own.
Changing your filter
Have you ever noticed that when you’re feeling lonely, you seem to see couples everywhere?
It feels like the whole world is against you: a pair of pigeons here, a cat and a kitten there, while you’re all alone. This is how a cognitive distortion works—a negative filter.
It’s a mistake in thinking and perception where you notice only what troubles you and ignore everything else.

Change your filter—look at the world more broadly. Learn to see not just happy couples, but also happy individuals. Or people who are in relationships but aren’t actually happier for it—social status doesn’t always deliver.

<q author="Henry David Thoreau">Happiness is like a butterfly: the more you chase it, the more it eludes you. But if you turn your attention to other things, it will come and quietly settle on your shoulder.</q>
The Anticipated Pleasure Sheet
Happiness can be found every day in small joys, in personal growth, in friendship, and in many other aspects of life.
But you likely don’t think this way, and you might be convinced that you can’t be happy without another person.

To test this belief against reality, use the “Anticipated Pleasure Sheet.” It contains several columns where you will predict and then record the actual level of pleasure you get from various activities (work or leisure) while alone or in the company of others.
• In the first column, enter the date of the experiment

• In the second, write down a few activities you plan to do that day as part of the experiment. (We recommend conducting 40–50 experiments over two to three weeks. Choose activities that usually bring you a sense of satisfaction or enjoyment, or those that have potential for learning or personal growth.)
• In the third column, note who you will be doing them with. If alone, write: “Me.”
<important>In the fourth column, estimate how much pleasure a specific activity will bring you on a scale of 0 to 100%—the higher the number, the higher the expected pleasure.</important>
• It is very important to fill in the fourth column BEFORE you start the activity, not after! Once you’ve filled in the first four columns, proceed to the activity.
Afterward, in the fifth column, record the actual level of pleasure using the same scale—from 0 to 100%.
By conducting a series of these experiments, you can analyze your data and learn many interesting things about yourself.
First, by comparing anticipated pleasure (column 4) with actual pleasure (column 5), you’ll see how accurate your predictions are.
<q author="Eleanor Roosevelt">No one can make you feel inferior without your consent.</q>
You might realize that you often underestimate the level of pleasure you expect to receive, especially when doing things alone.
You might also be surprised to find that being with someone doesn’t always live up to your expectations.
In fact, you might even discover that in many cases, spending time alone was more pleasant than being in company.
You may also see that the highest ratings you gave to solo activities are equal to, or even higher than, the ratings for activities done with others.
Reframing Beliefs
Love, relationships, and marriage aren’t prerequisites for happiness or self-esteem; sometimes, they simply aren’t enough.
The proof is in the millions of people who are married yet remain unhappy.
If love were a cure for loneliness, bad moods, or depression, then psychologists would be out of a job.
But unfortunately, that isn’t the case—having a partner doesn’t guarantee a happy life. This is something that needs to be recognized and accepted.
To start working with a belief, formulate it and write it down. It might sound like this:
• If I don’t have a partner, I am unhappy
• If I’m not loved, it means I’m a failure
• Without a relationship, I am incomplete
Next, describe exactly how this belief is holding you back. For example:
• endless, excessive demands on yourself, feeling like you’re not good enough for a relationship
• unrealistic expectations of a partner; making global conclusions about love instead of focusing on specific issues
• constant dissatisfaction and low mood, triggered by any situation involving being alone
After that, write down counterarguments. This can be a difficult process and may take more than one day—keep adding to your list as new thoughts come to mind.
For example, for the belief “Being alone is terrible and humiliating,” you could write the following counterarguments:
• being alone provides an opportunity to get to know oneself better
• being single offers the chance to try new things that would be much harder to do in a relationship
• it is better to be alone than to be with the wrong partner
And the most important part of this process is to replace your old belief with a new one. It should sound realistic and rational so that you can actually believe it.
For example: “Being alone can be pleasant and helpful; it’s a time to rest and get to know myself better. Love can manifest in many different types of relationships.

Even without a partner, I can feel closeness with people, share my experiences, and show warmth. I should focus on the kind of relationships I personally want, and if I don’t have them, set a goal to create them.
Not having a partner doesn’t make me incomplete, just as wanting a partner doesn’t make me weak or dependent.”
<important>Read these entries every day for 2–3 weeks; you can add to them or change them. This will help you overcome unhelpful thinking patterns and begin your transformation.</important>
Love is a wonderful experience, but like any other, it can be both positive and negative, and it shouldn’t define who we are or why we are here.
A desire and a need are not the same thing. Oxygen is a need, while love is a desire.
Love is not a basic human need!
It is perfectly normal to want to build a romantic relationship. There is nothing wrong with that. Having a good relationship with a loved one is a wonderful pleasure.
But to survive or to experience the highest levels of happiness, you don’t require anyone else’s approval, love, or attention.
